question.problem: Write $\frac{35{x}^{4}}{7{x}^{3}+2}$ in the form $ax+\frac{bx}{7{x}^{3}+2},$ where $a\ne 0.$ What is the value of $a+b?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we factor the numerator to put $7{x}^{3}$ in parentheses. Then, we add and subtract $2$ in the parentheses. This reveals a copy of the denominator without changing the value of the expression. 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{35{x}^{4}}{7{x}^{3}+2} & =\frac{5x(7{x}^{3})}{7{x}^{3}+2} \\  & =\frac{5x(7{x}^{3}+2-2)}{7{x}^{3}+2} \\  & =\frac{5x(7{x}^{3}+2)+5x(-2)}{7{x}^{3}+2} \\  & =\frac{5x(7{x}^{3}+2)-10x}{7{x}^{3}+2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we split the fraction into two, and then simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5x(7{x}^{3}+2)-10x}{7{x}^{3}+2} & =\frac{5x(7{x}^{3}+2)}{7{x}^{3}+2}+\frac{-10x}{7{x}^{3}+2} \\  & =5x+\frac{-10x}{7{x}^{3}+2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have $a=5$ and $b=-10,$ and we get

$$
a+b=5+(-10)=-5.
$$
